CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL ORDER

This criminal petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to quash proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 3 in Spl.C.No.73/2025, arising out of Crime No.134/2024, registered by Ferhatabad Police Station, for the offences NC: 2026:KHC-K:805 HC-KAR punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC, Section 6 of POCSO Act and Sections 9 and 11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, presently pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge and FTSC-1 (POCSO), Kalaburagi (for brevity "Trial Court").
2.
The factual matrix of the case is that, petitioners and respondent No.3 were working as Coolie on daily wage basis.
Petitioners No.1 hails from Melkunda(K) village and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are hails from the remote village of Mavanoor in Kalaburagi.

It is the case of prosecution that, on 12.11.2024 around 04.00 p.m., respondent No.2, who was an Anganwadi Supervisor, Town Circle,

2 Child Development Project Officer (CDPO), Kalaburagi Rural Municipality, based on the specific information, submitted a complaint before respondent No.1-Police that the petitioner No.1 married respondent No.3, who was aged about 17 years 9 months on 07.05.2022 and thereafter, respondent No.3 started to reside along with the petitioners.
Out of the wedlock, NC: 2026:KHC-K:805 HC-KAR respondent No.3 begotten a child.
Further allegation in the complaint is that, knowing fully aware that respondent No.3 was a minor, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 performed her marriage with petitioner No.1.

As such, based on the complaint of respondent No.2, the respondent No.1-Police registered the case against the petitioners in Crime No.134/2024 dated 12.11.2024 for the offences punishable under Section 9 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, Sections 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.

After completing the investigation the respondent No.1-Police laid charge sheet against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC,
Section 6 of POCSO Act and Sections 9 and 11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

Accordingly, the learned Special judge took cognizance of the offences and set up a trial and the prosecution has completed the examination of all the witnesses and case is posted for recording of 313 statement.
Hence challenging NC: 2026:KHC-K:805 HC-KAR the same, the petitioners filed this petition to quash the proceedings against them.

3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State.
4.
Apart from urging several contentions, the learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that,
since the petitioners are the rustic villagers and they have no such knowledge about the respondent No.3 was a minor at the time of incident.
Even otherwise, her age was 17 years 9 months and there are no such authenticated documents placed by the prosecution to prove that she was a minor at the time of incident.
In such circumstances, he submitted that, the proceedings against the petitioners is liable to be quashed.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

5. Per contra, the learned HCGP and the learned respondent No.3 jointly opposed the petition by NC: 2026:KHC-K:805 HC-KAR contending that, since already the prosecution has completed the examination of all the witnesses and case is set for recording of 313 statement, at this stage, there is no question of abuse of the process of Court by continuing the proceedings.
Hence, they pray to dismiss the petition.
6. I have given my anxious consideration both on the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the documents available on record.

7. As could be gathered from records, it is not seriously disputed by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the proceedings before the Trial Court in Special Case No.73/2025 is almost completed and the prosecution has completed the examination of all the witnesses and the case is posted for recording 313 statement.
At this juncture, as rightly contented by the learned counsel for the respondents, there is no question of abuse of the process of court by continuation of the proceedings.
Hence, liberty is to be reserved to the NC: 2026:KHC-K:805 HC-KAR petitioners to urge all their contentions before the Trial Court.

At this stage, the proceedings cannot be quashed,
since the trial has been almost completed.
